svg.font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: What Washington did and what the firms did on speech, competition, and privacy
svg.desc: A diagram in three rows, each with what Washington did on the left and what the firms did on the right. Speech: Washington shielded platforms from liability for what users post in 1996, and the firms decide what stays online. Competition: Washington enforced antitrust law lightly, and the firms, shown by the logos of Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta, and Microsoft, bought 770 startups in three decades. Privacy: Washington passed no comprehensive privacy law, and the firms collect users' data and sell targeted advertising.
